name: Phoenix
lede: Desert disc golf with water hazards and mountain views — from the iconic fountain course to a rugged 27 on the ridge. We're publishing the metro's best first.
introParagraphs: Phoenix disc golf trades the woods for wide-open desert and man-made lakes. Fountain Hills is the postcard — 20 holes around a lake beneath the iconic 300-foot fountain, with nine water hazards and the most photographed basket in Arizona. Buffalo Ridge is the rugged counterpart: 27 holes of elevation and blind throws alongside the mountain.

Paseo Vista in Chandler is the friendly former-landfill course, wide open and perfect for beginners, while Vista del Camino in Scottsdale is the classic park course with lakes in play on seven holes. The Phoenix Ladies League runs Sunday Funday events, and all of Phoenix's mapped courses are free to play.
New here? Paseo Vista to learn, Fountain Hills for the views, Buffalo Ridge for the workout. For gear, Disc Golf HQ and Spinners on the Green are the local pro shops.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in the Phoenix metro?
faqs.answer: There are 43 courses across the Phoenix metro, mapped and live on FindFrolf, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in Phoenix?
faqs.answer: Fountain Hills — the lake-side course beneath the iconic fountain with nine water hazards. Buffalo Ridge is the runner-up for players who want a mountain workout.

faqs.question: Are Phoenix's disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: Yes — every one of the 43 mapped courses is free to play.

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in Phoenix?
faqs.answer: Paseo Vista in Chandler — wide open, friendly, and great for learning distance control. Vista del Camino is another approachable classic.

faqs.question: Where can I buy disc golf gear in Phoenix?
faqs.answer: Disc Golf HQ is the dedicated pro shop. Spinners on the Green in Scottsdale carries a curated selection of discs and gear.
